title: Staggered Pulse A/B Orchestration — Scratchpad
body:
Purpose:
This scratchpad captures a lightweight, cross-functional protocol for running staggered pulse experiments (micro A/B injections across cohorts) intended to validate routing, metric safety gates, and rollback automation before larger rollouts. Not a final playbook — a working doc for iteration with ENG, SRE, Observability, and Product.
body_continued:
Key ideas (quick):
- Run very small, rapid pulses of traffic (0.1%–2%) across multiple microscopic cohorts rather than a single canary slice.
- Use coordinated, short-lived pulses to exercise end-to-end stacks (routing, KV cache, autoscale, fallback).
- Observe orthogonal signals: infra (latency/error budget), model quality (eval prompt set + user proxy), cost delta, and UX signals.
- Automate early aborts, but prefer manual approval for escalations until stable.

Design principles and constraints:
- Minimal blast radius per pulse: <=2% correlated user exposure across any single tenant.
- Pulse duration: 2–30 minutes depending on signal latency and downstream sampling. Start short, increase only for noisy metrics.
- Isolation: prefer synthetic traffic + real-user microcohorts where privacy and compliance allow.
- Cross-team ownership: product defines hypothesis/metric, eng owns routing, observability owns signal definitions, SRE owns abort/rollback automation.

Pulse types and when to use:
- smoke-pulse: 0.1% synthetic traffic, 2–5 min — validate endpoint + routing after deploy.
- traffic-pulse: 0.5%–1% real microcohorts, 10–15 min — validate latency/cost and basic quality.
- quality-pulse: 0.5% with pre-defined evaluation prompts interleaved — measure quality regressions.
- scale-pulse: 1%–2% synthetic burst to validate autoscaling and cache warmup.

Example cadence suggestion:
- Day 0 (post-deploy): smoke-pulse (automated) -> if green, schedule traffic-pulse within 2 hours.
- Within 24 hours: quality-pulse and scale-pulse in a controlled window.
- Week 1: repeated staggered pulses daily for first 3 days, then every other day until confidence.
runbook_steps:
Operator runbook (high-level):
1) Preflight checklist (10–15 min before):
   - Confirm hypothesis and success metrics (owner: Product).
   - Confirm pulse cohorts and sampling method (owner: Eng/Traffic Steward).
   - Confirm linked dashboards and alert thresholds (owner: Observability).
   - Notify stakeholders channel and on-call (owner: Pulse Owner).
2) Kickoff: create pulse ticket, start synthetic smoke-pulse.
3) Observe infra signals (p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, queue depth). If any threshold breached -> abort.
4) Observe quality signals (eval set passrate, semantic similarity fallback rate, user engagement proxies). If regression exceeds threshold -> pause and investigate.
5) If green, escalate to traffic-pulse with microcohorts.
6) After pulse finishes, record snapshot to pulse-log and run short analysis template.
7) If all checks pass across X iterations (configurable), mark rollout step as passed and proceed with higher exposure or rollout.

Safety gates and thresholds (examples, must be tuned per product):
- Infra: p95 latency increase > 25% OR 5xx rate increase > 0.25% -> abort.
- Cost: per-token cost increase > 30% for sustained >10 minutes -> alert product & SRE.
- Quality: eval precision drop > 5 percentage points OR increased fallback to low-qa model > 2x baseline -> pause.
- User proxy: engagement metric drop > 3% within pulse cohort -> investigate.

Signal instrumentation (obs owner checklist):
- Dedicated pulse dashboard with live baselining and comparison to last 24h.
- Short-window aggregations (1m/5m) and longer windows for drift (30m/2h).
- Tagging every request with pulse_id, cohort_id, and sampling_method.
- Automated snapshots saved to S3/metrics-store for postmortem analysis.

Roles and responsibilities (working):
- Pulse Owner (Product): writes hypothesis, success metrics, and approves pulses.
- Traffic Steward (Eng): defines cohorts and implements routing rules.
- Observability Lead (SRE/Obs): creates dashboards, defines thresholds, owns alerting.
- Oncall (SRE): executes aborts and rollback automation.
- Release Coordinator (Eng/Product): communicates status and runbook results.

Communication templates (examples):
Slack pre-pulse: "[pulse-id] Starting smoke-pulse for model XYZ at 12:05 UTC. Expected duration 5m. Owner @Aisha. Dashboards: <link>. Abort if p95 > X or 5xx > Y."
Slack abort: "[pulse-id] ABORTED: infra threshold breached (p95 X ms, 5xx Y%). Rolling back routing. Investigating @SRE-oncall."
Post-pulse summary (short): "pulse-id, duration, cohorts, infra verdict, quality verdict, actions (pass/hold/abort), followups, links to artifacts."

Sample size and estimation notes (very rough):
- For immediate signal detection (latency/errors) small cohorts suffice (N ~ 100–500 requests).
- For engagement/quality proxies you need more (N in thousands), so consider longer pulse or repeated pulses.
- When in doubt, layer synthetic evaluation prompts with deterministic expectations to get early quality signal without large user exposure.

Data capture and artifacts to save after each pulse:
- Raw request logs (tagged), aggregated metrics snapshots, eval results, sample of responses, routing config snapshot, autoscaler activity logs, and notes from humans on-call.

Postmortem and learning loop:
- Keep a lightweight pulse-log (CSV/Sheet) with one row per pulse: id, date, owner, cohort, outcome, top signals, tickets triggered.
- Weekly review of pulse-log in product/ops sync to capture flaky signals and adjust thresholds.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- How to standardize cohort naming across products without breaking privacy/tenant isolation?
- Can we automate a small-window statistical test for quality regressions that is robust at N<1k?
- How to integrate Dedicated and Private customers into pulses without violating contracts?
- Should abort thresholds be absolute or relative to rolling baseline?

Action items (next):
- Prototype smoke-pulse automation (Marcus) — include tagging and snapshotting.
- Obs: build the pulse dashboard template and alert rules (Leah).
- Product: enumerate 5 candidate hypotheses for the first pilot (Aisha).
- SRE: document rollback automation hooks and stub playbook (Omar).

Notes: this doc intentionally loose — prefer iteration and low-friction experiments. Keep pulses short and cheap, favor repeated exposure over single big canaries.

References and links:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.internal/pulse-framework-v1
- Pulse ticket template (Jira): JIRA-7891
- Example runbook repo: git+ssh://github.com/redwood/platform-pulse-runbook.git

---

Notes to self (quick scratch):
- Consider a "staggered heartbeat" variant where multiple micro-pulses trigger in sequence across different regions to test geo routing.
- Explore synthetic prompt-baseline harness that runs in parallel on every model change to deliver deterministic quality deltas in <2min.

End of scratchpad.
